title: MEPS 2017: people with a reported ICD-10 A69 (other spirochetal infections, which includes Lyme disease)
definition: People with at least one condition record whose 3-character ICD10CDX equals A69.
method: Sum of unique-person weights (PERWT17F) over the domain; standard error by Taylor linearisation over VARSTR/VARPSU. Person-level, one year only.
comparability: A69 is the broad category that contains Lyme (A69.2x); MEPS public files keep only the first 3 characters, so this is NOT a Lyme-specific count and must not be read as Lyme prevalence.
MEPS panels overlap across adjacent years: never add or pool these yearly totals.
Condition rows come from household reports coded by professional coders.

AHRQ (MEPS team, 2026-09-24) urges caution forming Lyme cost estimates from MEPS: pooling 2016-2024 gives only about 300-400 observations, expenditures are highly skewed (about 1,000 or more are needed for a solid mean), only treated Lyme is identified (zero-expenditure cases drop out, biasing upward), events may be flagged as arthritis without naming Lyme, comorbidities cannot be separated from Lyme, and onset dates are not recorded. Lyme-specific A69.2 is available only in restricted data centers.

uncertainty.note: Small samples give very wide, unreliable intervals.

summary: 2017: about 381,713 people (95% CI 207,906 to 555,520; 31 sampled persons) reported a condition coded A69.
how_to_use: Cross-check or population context only, never a prevalence of Lyme or Long COVID; not a cost estimate (events are counts, not dollars).

provenance.collection_note: Respondent-reported conditions and hours, coded to ICD-10 by MEPS abstractors; not a clinical record.
provenance.computed_by: Computed in code from the federal file; no AI model
provenance.relevance: A69 is the broad category that contains Lyme (A69.2x); MEPS public files keep only the first 3 characters, so this is NOT a Lyme-specific count and must not be read as Lyme prevalence.
provenance.reliability: 31 sampled persons with a design-based standard error.
